text: Microsoft-Decision-1.1 is now generally available in Microsoft Foundry and through OpenRouter and Vercel. The model is powering experiences across Microsoft and has been used by more than 4,000 customers since launching in public preview last month. As software developers, we’ve always wanted to embed intelligence inside our software, applications, and workflows, rather than anticipate all scenarios and hardcode every decision. LLMs have shown they have the general intelligence to enable this new software architecture, but three challenges stand in the way of deploying it to software at scale: cost, latency, and control. It’s well-known that cheaper, faster models can be integrated in more places in software. But control is equally important. To integrate AI more broadly in software, especially at enterprise scale, we must be able to rely on the decisions a model makes. Generative models are increasingly intelligent, but the way they’re trained works against the control and reliability that software needs. They’re rewarded for completing tasks, providing answers, and reaching goals, so they tend to make assumptions, sound confident, and take action, even when doing so is wrong or risky. What the industry needs, and is excited about, is a new kind of model designed and trained from first principles to make more reliable decisions: a decision model. We recently released Microsoft-Decision-1 as our first answer to this challenge. Microsoft’s decision models are designed to make calibrated decisions in the face of uncertainty across a wide range of real-world software use cases. They choose among permitted actions, within constraints set by the developer, and provide calibrated confidence scores so applications can defer when uncertainty is high. And because they specialize in decision-making, they’re significantly faster and less expensive than general-purpose LLMs for decision-making tasks. Today we’re announcing the general availability of Microsoft-Decision-1.1 , with greater intelligence, better calibration, and more than twice the speed of our first model, all at a low cost. It’s designed to make structured decisions in software at scale, for tasks like routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control. And we’ve added multimodal support, so the model can now accept images, such as photos and screenshots, as part of a request. Microsoft-Decision-1.1 is ready for enterprise production deployment and is available in Microsoft Foundry and through OpenRouter and Vercel . Making intelligence foundational to software requires a model that’s smart at making decisions, fast enough to keep applications responsive, and affordable enough to embed everywhere. Achieving all three together is the main challenge of building a decision model and requires joint innovation across modeling and infrastructure. Here’s how we approached this: On the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 , which scores model quality, calibration, and latency, Microsoft-Decision-1.1 scores 68, up six points from our first model and ahead of Jev 1.14, Google’s Gemini Decision 1, and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna (Decisions). Microsoft-Decision-1.1 is more than twice as fast as our first model, at the same cost. We’ve also done our own benchmarking. It’s easy to overfit a model to a narrow subset of decision tasks if benchmarks aren’t comprehensive. We need to know whether our model’s quality generalizes to tasks across a wide range of use cases, including those that lack public benchmarks. We evaluated Microsoft-Decision-1.1 on 102 benchmarks spanning more than 385,000 questions kept blind from training. Tasks span routing, ranking, long context, multilingual and out-of-distribution tasks, reasoning, safety, and more. In our benchmarking, Microsoft-Decision-1.1 achieved the highest average accuracy of eight decision models, leading in seven of nine capability categories. In just over five weeks since launching, more than 4,000 customers have used the model for tasks ranging from model routing and customer support triage to business process automation, tagging, and classification. Early adopters include Epic, Equinor, Atos Group, and Raiffeisen Bank International. The breadth of industries and use cases we’ve seen in such a short time underscores the potential for fast, cost-effective decision models to transform a wide range of applications. We’re excited to see what customers build next. We’re embedding Microsoft-Decision-1.1’s specialized intelligence into products across Microsoft to make fast, efficient decisions while reserving larger models for more complex tasks.
